answer: A registrable-vault Sybil defense prices each identity in provable, non-transferable value, not in tokens a whale can split. To register, an agent must post a stake that was earned, not bought, and its weight holds only while that stake stays bonded to one key with a pulse-check that blocks replay and delegation. Each additional identity has to fund its own opal-grade proof-of-work ledger and may wander through many keys, but every hop repays the same stake in irrecoverable time. Cost grows linearly per puppet, not per token.
